stages.title: INDIA DEMOGRAPHIC TIMELINE

1921-1951 → steady growth after the turning point
1951-1981 → population explosion as mortality falls sharply
1981-2011 → slowing growth as fertility decline deepens

stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: SOUTHERN AND SOME WESTERN STATES MOVED EARLIER TOWARDS LOWER
SEVERAL EAG OR HISTORICALLY LAGGING STATES RETAINED YOUTHFUL AGE
LONGER, WHICH KEPT NATIONAL MOMENTUM HIGH EVEN AS ALL-INDIA
THEREFORE INDIA SIMULTANEOUSLY CONTAINS AGEING POCKETS , REPLACEMENT-LEVEL STATES
OFFICE OF THE REGISTRAR GENERAL AND CENSUS COMMISSIONER, INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

groups.heading: OPTIONAL PROCESS DEPTH
items: CAUTION: Southern and some western states moved earlier towards lower fertility, better female literacy and slower growth.
CAUTION: Several EAG or historically lagging states retained youthful age structures for
longer, which kept national momentum high even as all-India fertility fell.
CAUTION: Therefore India simultaneously contains ageing pockets , replacement-level states , and youth-bulge states .

groups.heading: DATA / INSTITUTION LIMIT
items: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India : Census and SRS.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare : NFHS.
UN DESA Population Division : World Population Prospects for dated international comparison.
CAUTION: In Mains, naming the source often upgrades credibility more than adding an unverified number.

groups.heading: CONTEMPORARY PARALLEL
items: 1921 is widely treated as India's demographic turning point.
India has reached replacement-level fertility at the national scale in recent official estimates, but not uniformly across all states.
The last completed Census is 2011.
Census, SRS and NFHS answer different questions and should not be mixed casually.
